content.title: About
content.content: White chocolate candy is a small confection made from white chocolate, which consists of cocoa butter, sugar, milk solids, and vanilla. The candies have a delicate creamy flavor, a smooth texture, and are often enhanced with additional flavorings or sprinkles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White chocolate contains no cocoa solids, giving it a light color and a milder, milkier taste.
The first white chocolate was created in Switzerland in the early 1920s.
Candies are frequently molded into miniature shapes, making them popular for gifts and celebrations.
Flavorings such as mint, strawberry, or caramel are often added to diversify the taste.
White chocolate melts at a lower temperature than dark chocolate, which makes it easier to shape into candies.

items.title: Source of cocoa butter
items.content: Cocoa butter provides monounsaturated fatty acids that may support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: The milk components in white chocolate supply a modest amount of calcium, beneficial for bones.

items.title: Vitamins A and E
items.content: Vanilla and plant oils contribute antioxidants such as vitamin E.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The high sugar and fat content delivers rapid energy, useful during intense physical activity.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sugar and cocoa butter can stimulate serotonin production, helping to lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake may lead to weight gain, tooth decay, and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy should avoid white chocolate.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some manufacturers use partially hydrogenated oils that may contain trans fats.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: White chocolate candy is very calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candies can be enjoyed on their own, added to ice cream, baked goods, or used as decorative toppings for cakes. They are also convenient as a quick sweet snack on the go.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep them refrigerated to prevent melting and texture changes.
